class.name: CgameTradeJournal
class.brief_description: Crash-safe redo log for two-account deals such as trades and market sales.
class.description: [CgameTradeJournal] stores the post-deal snapshots (after-images) of both characters of a deal on disk before the backend commits the pair, so a crash between "deal done in memory" and "backend confirmed" can be replayed on restart with the same transaction id. A side becomes superseded once a later save of that account succeeded: its snapshot is older than the backend and must never be written back. [method replay_kind] tells which sides of an entry are still newest. The journal is rewritten through a temporary file and an atomic rename. A corrupt journal makes [method open_file] fail instead of guessing. All public methods lock an internal recursive mutex.

method.name: open_file
method.description: Opens (or creates) the journal at [param journal_path] and loads its entries. Returns [code]false[/code] if the file is corrupt, has an unknown version or cannot be written.

method.name: valid_entry
method.description: Returns whether [param entry] has the shape of a journal entry.

method.name: record
method.description: Journals a deal before it is committed. Returns [code]false[/code] if it could not be made durable, the transaction id is empty or the journal holds [constant MAX_ENTRIES] entries.

method.name: settle
method.description: Removes a confirmed or replayed deal.

method.name: supersede
method.description: Marks the journaled sides of an account as stale after a newer save landed. Deals with both sides superseded are dropped.

method.name: replay_kind
method.description: Returns [code]"pair"[/code] when both sides are newest, [code]"single"[/code] when only one is, otherwise [code]"none"[/code].

method.name: accounts
method.description: Returns every account that appears in an unsettled deal.

members.member: Journal file. An empty path keeps the journal in memory.
Unsettled deals keyed by transaction id: [code]a[/code] and [code]b[/code] sides ([code]user[/code], [code]data[/code], [code]superseded[/code]) and [code]time[/code].
